policy.honest_boundary: Nix-provided binaries live in /nix/store by construction: their RPATHs and ELF interpreter paths are absolute store paths, so they CANNOT be relocated under toolchains/ and still execute. toolchains/nix-profile is a symlink farm into the store, not a copy. Any claim that the Nix binaries are physically inside the project is false.

defects_closed_in_this_pass: tools/lib/uos-toolchain.sh resolved UOS_ROOT from ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} under `set -euo pipefail`. guards.nix_flake_check: checks.x86_64-linux.toolchain-pin -- a runCommand that fails the FLAKE (not merely a shell) unless the pinned erl exists, reports OTP 29, and has not escaped the store into /usr or /home. guards.devenv_enterTest: Three arms, each catching what the others cannot: [release] otp_release == 29; [derivation] readlink -f $(command -v erl) == the pinned store path; [profile parity] toolchains/nix-profile/bin/erl resolves to that SAME derivation, which is what catches devenv.lock and flake.lock drifting apart. Verified PASS; profile parity confirmed both resolve /nix/store/96cqahwqjxzx4pywz1bj53apncjmhhdg-erlang-29.0.5.
guards.uos_toolchain_verify: New shell function. Three arms: presence, LOCALITY (no entrypoint resolving under $HOME, /usr, /opt or /home/an/dev/ver/*), and BEAM (OTP 29 and store-resolved). This is the arm that would have caught release_process.ml. Deliberately does NOT hardcode a store path: identity is the flake's authority, locality is the shell's, and a third source of truth would drift.
guards.ocaml_tool_table_parity: release_process.ml now carries an OCaml resolver mirroring the shell table, plus a parity guard that text-parses tools/lib/uos-toolchain.sh (no shell executed, preserving the file's argv-only discipline) and fails closed on any divergence. 22 arms compared.

guards.preflight_scope: toolchain_preflight() runs before EVERY release_process.ml command, not only a dedicated one: a file that once silently used an unpinned BEAM does not get to opt in to being checked.
